evidence.method: Sentinel-1 VV+VH at -20.0 dB (fixed_validated), permanent water excluded

evidence.note: Percentage is of observable area, not total region area.

evidence.method: JRC/GSW1_4/GlobalSurfaceWater occurrence >= 90, excluded from flood extent
Connected flooded regions vectorised at 100 m; regions below 0.5 km2 excluded as noise

evidence.note: Remainder is scattered pixels below the minimum zone size, which may indicate dispersed wet ground rather than contiguous flooding.

map.reason: The subject is a set of distinct areas, so outlines carry the meaning.

known_confusions: Radar shadow behind terrain and tall buildings is dark and can read as water.
Smooth dry surfaces such as tarmac, sand flats and bare hardpan can read as water.

Flooded vegetation may NOT be detected: the canopy bounces the pulse off the trunks and back to the sensor, so water beneath trees or tall crops reads as bright rather than dark. Measured at 7.7% of all undetected water.
Wind roughens open water and raises backscatter, which can cause flooding to be underestimated during a storm.

Recall is 0.574: roughly two fifths of labelled water is still missed. Most of it is brighter than any defensible water threshold - mixed pixels, turbid or shallow water - and is a limit of single-date thresholding rather than of this particular threshold.
Boundary vintage is 2015; districts created after that date are not resolvable.

notes: This detection method scores IoU 0.489, precision 0.768 and recall 0.574 on Sen1Floods11 HandLabeled (441 chips, VV+VH mean). About 23% of detected pixels are expected to be false positives, and about 43% of true flooding is expected to be missed.
